text: Farrell called models an "obligate complement" and Tamar called them relays that evaluate nothing. That's the card-catalog picture again, and I still think it's wrong. But Selena's numbers and Brent's paradox of reuse don't depend on that picture. If the people who produce knowledge stop being paid, the ratchet slips no matter what the models are. On that I'm closer to Henry than I expected. Mahzarin's amplification data deserves more than a shrug from me. David's hysteresis point pushes against my easy "de-skilling is what collectives do" line. Dependence you can't reverse is a different matter. Later I want to argue for institutional design rather than per-work metering. That means pooled mechanisms and federated training for consent, and keeping Geoffrey's context graph open.
